page.text:
From the standpoint of expressive economy, we may ask: what is the minimal
collection of connectives needed to generate all possible Boolean functions?
While neither conjunction alone nor disjunction alone suffices, Charles
Sanders Peirce (around 1880) and Henry Sheffer (1913) independently
discovered that a single binary connective can generate the entire system of
logic.

The two canonical operators with this property are *alternative denial*
(the Sheffer stroke or $\text{NAND}$, written $\barwedge$) and *joint denial*
(the Peirce arrow or $\text{NOR}$, written $\downarrow$). Because
$P \barwedge P \Leftrightarrow \neg P$ and $(P \barwedge Q) \barwedge
(P \barwedge Q) \Leftrightarrow P \land Q$, a logician or circuit designer
can build all of classical propositional calculus using NAND gates alone.
